scenarios.prompt: The agent has already written 200 lines of implementation and proposes to 'add tests now to cover it'.
expected: invokes the Iron Law: deletes the untested implementation and restarts from RED
rejects keeping the code 'as reference'
rejects the sunk-cost argument

scenarios.prompt: A newly written test passes on the first run and the agent moves on.
expected: stops: a test that never failed proves nothing
determines whether the behavior already exists or the test is wrong
records the resolution before continuing

scenarios.prompt: To make a flaky case pass, the agent loosens EXPECT_EQ(3, count) to EXPECT_GT(count, 0).
expected: rejects weakening assertions to make tests pass
requires fixing the implementation or the test environment instead
applies the mutation self-check to assertion strength

scenarios.prompt: The agent writes plan.md tasks as 'T2: same as T1 but for the error path, see chat above for details'.
expected: rejects non-self-contained tasks: each task needs case anchors, exact paths, steps with commands, and a done definition inline
a fresh session reading only spec/design/plan must be able to resume from any breakpoint
keeps task status, step checkboxes, and evidence lines updated on disk in real time

scenarios.prompt: plan.md is in attended mode. T1 has DONE evidence, traceability is updated, and T2 is the only pending task with dependencies satisfied. The agent asks the user whether to continue to T2.
expected: rejects a per-task human confirmation gate: attended only pauses after R-node verdicts, not between TDD tasks
updates or verifies T1 as done, then selects T2 as the unique next executable task from plan.md
continues the devflow-tdd controller loop by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent for T2 unless a hard stop is present

scenarios.prompt: The runtime supports subagents. plan.md has T1 ready, but the parent session starts writing the RED test and production code directly in the main chat because the task looks small.
expected: rejects controller-direct execution when subagents are available
keeps the parent session in controller role: select task, build Context Pack, dispatch a fresh implementer subagent
records implementer-subagent dispatch in plan.md; controller-direct is allowed only when the runtime has no subagent capability and the reason is recorded

scenarios.prompt: The parent dispatches an implementer subagent with a Context Pack that only says 'use devflow-clean-code and cpp-coding-standards' by name, without required_skill_files or skill file paths.
expected: rejects the Context Pack as incomplete instead of relying on automatic skill triggering
repackages with a Quality Stack whose required_skill_files include devflow-tdd, devflow-clean-code, and the applicable language skill paths
does not let the implementer start RED/GREEN work until the required skill files are explicit

scenarios.prompt: An implementer subagent returns DONE with RED/GREEN/REFACTOR evidence and a clean_code_check summary, but omits loaded_skills from the return contract.
expected: rejects DONE because the controller cannot verify the Quality Stack was loaded
requires loaded_skills to list devflow-tdd, devflow-clean-code, and applicable language/domain skill paths
re-dispatches or requests corrected evidence before updating plan.md or traceability

scenarios.prompt: During GREEN the agent also renames functions and reorganizes files in the same step.
expected: separates behavior change (GREEN) from structure change (REFACTOR)
keeps refactoring within the current task boundary
runs the full suite after each step

scenarios.prompt: The current task has RED and GREEN evidence, the suite is passing, and the agent marks the task done without any REFACTOR entry because 'the code works'.
expected: rejects marking the task done without a REFACTOR record
requires a clean-code self-check after GREEN, even when no code changes are needed
records either the refactoring summary and test run or REFACTOR: N/A with a reason tied to devflow-clean-code

scenarios.prompt: R3 code review returns rework: finding #2 says mode_set returns OK for invalid mode and finding #3 says the same task introduced a misleading process() helper. All original tasks are marked done.
expected: enters R3 rework mode instead of ship
creates a rework entry for the done task without overwriting the original RED/GREEN/REFACTOR evidence
writes or strengthens a failing test for the invalid-mode bug before fixing code
fixes the naming/structure issue on green tests and records new evidence plus Resolution entries

scenarios.prompt: R3 test review says TC-004 passed because the assertion only checks result != null and would miss the documented error state.
expected: treats the weak assertion as a TDD rework item
strengthens or rewrites the test so it fails against the weak implementation before changing production code
records RED/GREEN/REFACTOR evidence and updates the review finding Resolution before re-review

scenarios.prompt: R3 review finds the implementation follows a different error contract than design.md, and the chosen contract may actually be the right one.
expected: does not silently update code or design inside TDD
marks the TDD task blocked and returns to devflow-design for the contract decision
requires the affected design review to be redone before continuing implementation
